'''''Eucalyptus globulus'' subsp. ''bicostata''''', commonly known as  the '''southern blue gum''', '''eurabbie''', '''blue gum''' or '''Victorian blue gum''',<ref name="CANBR">{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus globulus'' subsp. ''bicostata''|url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/euclid/text/entities/eucalyptus_globulus_subsp._bicostata.htm|website=keyserver.lucidcentral.org|publisher=Centre for Australian Biodiversity Research|access-date=2 June 2020}}</ref> is a subspecies of tree that is [[Endemism|endemic]] to south-eastern Australia. It has mostly smooth bark with some persistent slabs of old bark at the base, juvenile leaves with one [[wikt:glaucous#Adjective|glaucous]] side, glossy, lance-shaped adult leaves, warty flower buds in groups of three, white flowers and hemispherical to conical fruit.[[File:Eucalyptus bicostata - umbels.jpg|thumb|225px|Characteristic 3-budded umbels]]

==Description==
''Eucalyptus globulus'' subsp. ''bicostata'' is a tree that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|45|m}} and forms a [[lignotuber]]. The bark is mostly smooth, shedding in long strips to leave a white or greyish surface. There is sometimes rough, partially shed bark at the base of the trunk and ribbons of shedding bark in the upper branches. Young plants and [[coppice]] regrowth have stems that are more or less square in cross-section, with a prominent wing on each corner. The juvenile leaves are [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]], arranged in opposite pairs, elliptic to egg-shaped, the lower surface covered by a white, waxy bloom, {{cvt|40-115|mm}} long and {{cvt|22-60|mm}} wide. Adult leaves are arranged alternately, glossy green, lance-shaped to curved, {{cvt|140-400|mm}} long and {{cvt|20-60|mm}} wide on a [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] {{cvt|30-60|mm}} long.<ref name="CANBR"/><ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |last1=Brooker |first1=M. Ian H. |last2=Slee |first2=Andrew V. |title=''Eucalyptus globulus'' subsp. ''bicostata'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/bee23fee-60b5-4830-8d72-b3b796a28876 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref><ref name="ABRS">{{cite web |last1=Chippendale |first1=George M. |title=''Eucalyptus globulus'' subsp. ''bicostata'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Eucalyptus%20globulus%20subsp.%20bicostata |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of the Environment and Energy, Canberra |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref>

The flower buds are arranged in groups of three in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s on a thick [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]]  {{cvt|1-3|mm}} long, the individual buds more or less sessile. Mature buds are glaucous, conical and warty,{{cvt|10-18|mm}} long and {{cvt|10-14|mm}} wide with two ribs along the sides and a flattened [[Operculum (botany)|operculum]] that has a central knob. Flowering mainly occurs between January and March and the flowers are white. The fruit is a woody, sessile, hemispherical to conical [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{cvt|7-10|mm}} long and {{cvt|13-22|mm}} wide with two longitudinal ridges and the valves at about rim level.<ref name="CANBR"/><ref name="RBGV" /><ref name="ABRS" />

==Taxonomy and naming==
Southern blue gum was first formally described by [[Joseph Henry Simmonds]] in the book ''Trees from other lands for shelter and timber in New Zealand: Eucalypts'' and given the name ''Eucalyptus bicostata''.<ref name=APNI1>{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus bicostata''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/454559|publisher=APNI|access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref> In 1974, [[James Barrie Kirkpatrick]] reduced ''E. bicostata'' to the subspecies, ''E. globulus'' subsp. ''bicostata''.<ref name="K.B.Kirk.">{{cite journal |last1=Kirkpatrick |first1=James Barrie |title=The numerical intraspecific taxonomy of ''Eucalyptus globulus'' Labill. (Myrtaceae) |journal=The Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |date=September 1974 |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=89–104|doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.1974.tb01618.x }}</ref> The change has been accepted by the [[Australian Plant Census]].<ref name="APC" />
The epithet ''bicostata'' is derived from the Latin ''bicostatus'', "two-ribbed", referring to the buds and fruit.<ref name="CANBR"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
Southern blue gum grows in open forest in mountainous, largely inland country in New South Wales and Victoria. It is found between the [[Carrai National Park]] on the [[Northern Tablelands]] of New South Wales and the ranges of eastern Victoria.<ref name="RBGV" />
